title: Security Group Without Public SSH
scenario: Lock down a security group: allow HTTPS from the internet, never SSH from 0.0.0.0/0.

focus.title: Complete the aws_security_group resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_security_group.

hints.why: EC2 teaches the core lifecycle of compute: image, instance type, networking, storage and safe replacement.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_security_group" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_security_group. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use EC2 when you need a virtual machine you control directly, or as a building block inside an autoscaling or container platform.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_security_group" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; description; vpc_id; ingress { from_port; to_port; protocol; cidr_blocks }; ingress {}; egress { from_port; to_port; protocol; cidr_blocks }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.vpc_id`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
